newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - M. Stanley boosts Kulicke.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - M. Stanley boosts Kulicke.

text.p: -- Morgan Stanley analyst Jay Deanna said he raised his rating on semiconductor equipment maker Kulicke & Soffa Industries Inc to strong buy from outperform, boosted his earnings estimates and set a new target price.
-- Deanna said he boosted his 12-month price target to $30 from $25. The stock was up 2-3/4 to 24-7/8 in early trading Thursday.

-- The analyst said he raised his estimate for the first quarter ended in December to a profit of $0.02 per share from $0.01 per share. The Wall Street consensus prior to his move called for the company to report a loss of $0.03 per share.

-- He said he raised his estimate for the fiscal year ending September 1997 to $1.45 from $1.15 per share and his fiscal 1998 estimate to $2.25 from $2.00 per share. The analysts' consensus had been $0.71 per share for FY97.
-- "I am trying to lead the charge here," Deanna said of his aggressive earnings estimates.

-- "They experienced strong bookings in the December quarter and are continuing to do so" in the current period, he said, adding that, "I think we have increased visibility for the third and fourth quarters of 1997 now."

-- He described his investment thesis as a "volume unit play" reflecting the rapid rise in semiconductor production volumes, the tightening of industry capacity and the resultant demand for new equipment.

-- "Also it is an Intel play," Deanna noted. He said he expected the company to derive up to 20 percent of its revenues in fiscal 1997 from supplying Intel with assembly equipment, up from 12 percent or so in fiscal 1996.
-- He said a near-term catalyst for the stock could be the realease of semiconductor equipment industry book-to-bill figures on January 17.
-- While he expected the industry as a whole to see a bookings ratio of 0.90 to 0.97, he expected the assembly segment of the industry to come in at 1.15 or higher.
-- He noted that Kulicke and Soffa holds about one-half of the market share in the semiconductor device assembly category.
